subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw status falsely reports openclaw-mem0 memory as unavailable when the live gateway plugin is working

question: Should OpenClaw status use live gateway memory-runtime health as the source of truth for enabled external memory plugins, or is the current `not checked` behavior sufficient outside `status --all`?
rationale: Current main removes the worst wording but does not satisfy the requested live-runtime health contract, and the open fork PR plus the broader related issue need an owner decision before another fix path is queued.

options.title: Use live gateway status as canonical
options.body: Make the broader live-gateway memory status contract canonical, close or replace the conflicting fork PR, and require live external-memory proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Revive the fork PR
options.body: Ask the fork PR author to rebase, resolve conflicts, and prove `status --deep` plus JSON output against a real external memory plugin without local startup side effects.

options.title: Accept `not checked`
options.body: Declare the current softened status wording sufficient, close the fork PR, and update docs/tests if `--deep` is not meant to report memory runtime health.

recommendation.title: Use live gateway status as canonical
recommendation.body: Make the broader live-gateway memory status contract canonical, close or replace the conflicting fork PR, and require live external-memory proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the most recent concrete history on the shared memory status snapshot path that would need to be reconciled with the live-gateway contract.
